title: Basin mean removal changed the rank of the 2020-2025 North Pacific SST mean under fixed EOF tests
abstract: We tested how mean removal affects a selected low North Pacific sea surface temperature projection. We fitted an area-weighted leading spatial pattern to globally demeaned ERSSTv5 in 1950-2019, then kept its pattern and scale fixed. The 2020-2025 mean was -1.073, below all 65 January-start six-year means within 1950-2019. Removing the North Pacific mean instead gave -0.905, above two earlier means. A uniform basin-minus-global component gave 15.7% of the recent negative projection. Most of the negative value remained in the spatial contrast. A separately fitted contrast pattern put four earlier means below the recent value. The uniform share ranged from 1.2% to 25.3% with the fitting period. Thus a record-low rank is sensitive to index definition. This is a geometric test of one revised SST field and a known interval. It does not establish a regime change or attribute warming to a cause. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and a figure are included. External raw data remain outside the package.

display.caption: A fixed SST projection splits into a basin contrast and a uniform basin-minus-global part. Mean removal changes the recent six-year rank in the primary case. Gray points are overlapping earlier windows; orange diamonds are 2020-2025 means.
